mainTopic: Which תנא our משנה follows on watering fields, whether weeding and watering on שבת count as plowing or sowing, and how watering can be allowed in שביעית.
overview: The גמרא finishes a suggestion that רבי יהודה forbids watering a rain-fed field (בית הבעל) only from a brand-new spring that might collapse. It rejects that idea, because then our משנה would match no תנא. So for רבי יהודה only the type of field matters, and the ברייתא mentions a new spring only to show how far רבי מאיר goes. Next, רבה says weeding or watering on שבת counts as plowing (חורש), and רב יוסף says it counts as sowing (זורע). אביי asks both why it is not both, and that difficulty stands. רב יוסף then challenges רבה from a ברייתא about weeding כלאים, and the גמרא defends רבה: the lashes are for keeping the mixture growing (מקיים), as רבי עקיבא learns from the פסוק. Finally the גמרא asks how our משנה can allow watering in שביעית. אביי answers that the משנה means שביעית today, which according to רבי is only rabbinic. רבא begins a second answer that works even for the רבנן, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה's limit is only about a new spring that might collapse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a suggestion that רבי יהודה forbids watering a rain-fed field only from a new spring, because it may cave in. From an older, stable spring he would allow even a rain-fed field.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because it might collapse. But a spring that did not just come out, which will not collapse, may be used even for a rain-fed field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to the idea that our משנה follows רבי יהודה. It suggests that רבי יהודה's limit applies only to a brand-new spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newly emerged spring has weak walls, so heavy use might make it collapse. The suggestion is that this danger is the only reason רבי יהודה forbids watering a בית הבעל. If so, an old, stable spring would be allowed even for a rain-fed field.

keyTerms.meaning: a spring that has just started flowing (newly emerged)
a field that gets enough water from rain

phrases.english: because it might come to collapse.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a brand-new spring. Its walls are still weak and could cave in.

phrases.english: But a spring that did not just emerge,
which will not come to collapse —
even a rain-watered field may be watered too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion from before this section that challenges matching the משנה to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה's limit comes only from the danger of collapse, he would allow a rain-fed field from an old spring. The משנה does not seem to allow that.

steps.title: Then whose view is our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: if it were true, our משנה would match no תנא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, to whom will you attribute our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from Step 1. That reading would leave our משנה with no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists both new and old springs and permits only a thirsty field. רבי מאיר permits even a rain-fed field, so the משנה is not his view. Under the suggestion, רבי יהודה would permit a rain-fed field from an old spring, so it would not be his view either.

keyTerms.meaning: on whom will you place it? (whose view is it?)

phrases.english: If so —
to whom will you attribute our Mishnah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion made in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה distinguishes between new and old springs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would leave our משנה matching neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion in Step 1 that רבי יהודה forbids a rain-fed field only from a newly emerged spring.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that reading our משנה, which allows only a thirsty field even from an old spring, would match neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה makes no difference between springs
steps.stepSummary: Rather, for רבי יהודה the type of spring does not matter; only the type of field does. The ברייתא mentions a new spring only to show how far רבי מאיר's leniency goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רבי יהודה it makes no difference whether the spring is new or old. A thirsty field may be watered; a rain-fed field may not. The ברייתא mentions a new spring to show the strength of רבי מאיר's view: even from a new spring, one may water even a rain-fed field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the suggestion aside and goes back to matching our משנה with רבי יהודה. It also explains why the ברייתא spoke about a new spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the only question is whether the field truly needs the water. The age of the spring plays no role. The ברייתא chose the case of a new spring because that is where רבי מאיר's leniency is most striking: he permits watering even a rain-fed field from a spring that might collapse.

keyTerms.meaning: a thirsty field that needs irrigation
to show you how far his view goes

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה. A thirsty field may be watered from any spring, and a rain-fed field may not. רבי מאיר permits even a rain-fed field, even from a new spring.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה's rule depends on the spring being new. The ברייתא mentions a new spring only to highlight רבי מאיר's leniency.

phrases.english: Rather: according to Rabbi Yehuda
there is no difference between a spring that just emerged

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מַעְיָין שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא בַּתְּחִילָּה,
phrases.english: and a spring that did not just emerge;
a field that needs irrigation — yes,
a rain-watered field — no.
And the fact that it teaches about a spring that just emerged
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue.

phrases.english: is to tell you how far Rabbi Meir's view goes,
that even from a spring that is just emerging —
one may water from it even a rain-watered field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 2 rejects the suggestion, 'אלא' gives the correct reading of רבי יהודה. This answers Step 1's challenge, so our משנה does follow רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the opinion and explaining why the ברייתא chose its case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's limit depended on the spring being new.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה only the type of field matters. The new spring in the ברייתא is there to show רבי מאיר's strength.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that our משנה follows רבי יהודה's view on watering in חול המועד.

steps.title: Weeding and watering on שבת: plowing or sowing?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: for weeding or watering plants on שבת, what מלאכה is named in the warning? רבה says חורש (plowing); רב יוסף says זורע (sowing).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: someone who weeds or waters seedlings on שבת — for which מלאכה do we warn him? רבה said: plowing. רב יוסף said: sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute between אמוראים. The question is which category of forbidden work weeding and watering fall under.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a court can punish someone, he must be warned and told the exact sin he is about to do. On שבת, that means naming the specific מלאכה. רבה and רב יוסף disagree whether this work counts as plowing or as sowing.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who weeds or one who waters seedlings on Shabbat,
for what do we warn him?
Rabba said: for plowing.
Rav Yosef said: for sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר הַמְנַכֵּשׁ וְהַמַּשְׁקֶה מַיִם לִזְרָעִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from watering in חול המועד to watering on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: weeding and watering fall under חורש. רב יוסף: they fall under זורע.

steps.title: רבה's reasoning: it loosens the soil
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that plowing loosens the earth, and weeding and watering loosen the earth too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: My view makes sense. Plowing works by loosening the earth, and this also loosens the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the reason for his view that weeding and watering count as plowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looks at what the action does to the ground. Pulling out weeds or soaking the soil softens it, which is exactly what plowing is for.

keyTerms.meaning: it is logical according to my own view

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is logical according to my view:
just as the way of plowing
is to loosen the earth,
this too loosens the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבה's reasoning for his view in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that weeding and watering are חורש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: like plowing, these actions loosen the soil.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reasoning: it makes the plant grow
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that sowing makes produce grow, and weeding and watering also make produce grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: My view makes sense. Sowing works by making produce grow, and here too this makes produce grow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the reason for his view that weeding and watering count as sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף looks at the result for the plant. Weeding and watering help the crop grow, which is exactly what sowing is for.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה looks at the effect on the soil (loosening it, like plowing). רב יוסף looks at the effect on the plant (helping it grow, like sowing).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is logical according to my view:
just as the way of sowing
is to make the produce grow,
here too it makes the produce grow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רב יוסף's reasoning beside רבה's reasoning in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that weeding and watering are זורע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: like sowing, these actions make the plant grow.

steps.title: אביי challenges both רבה and רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבה that both his view and רב יוסף's view are hard to accept, because weeding and watering fit both חורש and זורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: Your view is difficult, and רב יוסף's view is difficult. Your view is difficult: does he get warned for plowing and not for sowing? רב יוסף's view is difficult: does he get warned for sowing and not for plowing?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks both sides of the argument at once. He says each one picked only one מלאכה, but the action really fits both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said weeding and watering loosen the earth, so they are חורש. רב יוסף said they make plants grow, so they are זורע. אביי points out that both reasons are true together, so why should either one leave out the other מלאכה?

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, in your view

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
According to you, it is difficult,
and according to Rav Yosef, it is difficult.
According to you, it is difficult:
for plowing, yes,
phrases.notes: He means: you say the person is warned for plowing.

phrases.english: but for sowing, no?
According to Rav Yosef, it is difficult:
for sowing, yes,
but for plowing, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: לְדִידָךְ קַשְׁיָא וּלְרַב יוֹסֵף קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the two reasons given in steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבה (only חורש) and רב יוסף (only זורע).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weeding and watering both loosen soil and help growth, so both reasons apply at once; neither opinion should exclude the other מלאכה.

steps.title: Blocking the defense that one act brings only one liability
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects a possible answer, that one action can only bring one liability, by quoting רב כהנא: one who prunes and needs the wood is liable for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: wherever there are two, a person is liable for only one. But רב כהנא said: one who prunes and needs the wood is liable for two, one for planting and one for reaping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines how רבה and רב יוסף might defend themselves, and then knocks that defense down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible defense: even if an action fits two מלאכות, you are only liable for one, so each named just one. רב כהנא's case proves otherwise: pruning helps the vine grow (like planting) and also cuts wood he wants (reaping), and he is liable for both.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a possible answer

phrases.english: And if you say:
wherever there are two [forbidden labors in one act],
one is liable for only one,
but didn't Rav Kahana say:
one who prunes and needs the wood
is liable for two.
One for planting,
and one for reaping.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא תַּרְתֵּי לָא מִיחַיַּיב אֶלָּא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible answer to אביי's challenge in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested rule that one act can bring only one liability.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב כהנא rules that pruning for wood brings two liabilities, so one act can count as two מלאכות.

steps.title: The difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that אביי's challenge is not answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this round by saying the question has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying קשיא here means the problem stays open for both רבה and רב יוסף. It is not a full rejection, but no answer is given.
steps.whatToRemember: Weeding and watering seem to fit both חורש and זורע, and the גמרא leaves the challenge to both opinions unanswered.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of steps 7 and 8 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's challenge to both views remains unresolved.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא about mixed seeds against רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: one who weeds or covers roots of כלאים gets lashes, and רבי עקיבא adds even one who keeps them growing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged רבה: One who weeds or covers roots for mixed seeds gets lashes. רבי עקיבא says: even one who keeps them growing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף opens a new challenge against רבה by quoting a ברייתא. This sets up the next move, where the point of the challenge will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids sowing mixed seeds, yet this ברייתא gives lashes for weeding. That suggests weeding counts as sowing (זורע), which supports רב יוסף and seems to go against רבה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef challenged Rabba:
One who weeds or covers [roots] for mixed seeds
gets lashes.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Even one who keeps [them growing].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question to both, רב יוסף now attacks רבה alone with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that weeding falls under חורש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes for weeding כלאים, which is a sowing prohibition, suggest weeding counts as זורע.

steps.title: Plowing has no connection to כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that the ברייתא fits his view that weeding is like sowing, because sowing כלאים is forbidden. On רבה's view that weeding is like plowing, the lashes make no sense, because plowing is not forbidden with כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for me, since I say weeding is like sowing. That explains the lashes, because sowing כלאים is forbidden. But you say weeding is like plowing. Is plowing forbidden with כלאים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף now spells out the challenge from the ברייתא he quoted. The ברייתא fits his own view, but it seems to go against רבה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says one who weeds כלאים gets lashes. If weeding counts as זורע, the lashes make sense, because the Torah forbids sowing כלאים. If weeding counts as חורש, there is no source for lashes, because the Torah never forbids plowing in connection with כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / granted (opens a 'this fits, but that doesn't' challenge)
Forbidden mixtures of seeds grown together
Is it forbidden? (a question that expects the answer no)

phrases.english: It works well according to me,
since I say it is because of sowing:
phrases.notes: He means that weeding on שבת counts as sowing. That was רב יוסף's view.

phrases.english: that is why, since sowing is forbidden with כלאים.
But according to you, who said it is because of plowing:
phrases.notes: "You" is רבה, who held that weeding counts as plowing.

phrases.english: is plowing forbidden with כלאים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in step 10 to attack רבה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that weeding counts as חורש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives lashes for weeding כלאים. Only sowing, not plowing, is forbidden with כלאים, so the ברייתא must treat weeding as sowing.

steps.title: רבה: the lashes are for maintaining the כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the lashes in the ברייתא are not for plowing at all. They are for maintaining (מקיים) the forbidden mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is because of maintaining.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רב יוסף. The weeder gets lashes for keeping the כלאים growing, not for any kind of plowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה takes the ברייתא off the question of חורש versus זורע. The weeder is punished because he helps the forbidden mixture survive, which is a separate prohibition. So the ברייתא is no proof against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who maintains, meaning he keeps forbidden כלאים growing

phrases.english: He said to him: Because of maintaining.
phrases.notes: רבה is speaking. Weeding helps the כלאים keep growing, and that is what earns the lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes for weeding כלאים must come from the weeding being an act of sowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lashes come from maintaining the כלאים, so the ברייתא says nothing about חורש versus זורע.

steps.title: The ברייתא's ending suggests the first opinion is not about maintaining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבה's answer. רבי עקיבא adds 'even one who maintains,' which suggests the תנא קמא's lashes are not for maintaining.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches: 'רבי עקיבא says: even one who maintains.' This shows that the תנא קמא's reason is not maintaining!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's answer by reading the ברייתא closely. The extra words 'even one who maintains' seem to make מקיים a separate, new opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף ('even') shows that רבי עקיבא is adding something the תנא קמא did not say. So the תנא קמא must give lashes for weeding for another reason, which brings back the question of sowing versus plowing.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: But since it teaches in the last part:
Rabbi Akiva says: even one who maintains,
this implies that for the first Tanna
it is not because of maintaining!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the תנא קמא gives lashes for מקיים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's 'even' adds מקיים as a new point, so the תנא קמא's lashes must have a different reason.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא and explains its own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the whole ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא. The last part is not a separate opinion. It gives the reason for the first part: weeders get lashes for maintaining, as רבי עקיבא holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is רבי עקיבא, and it is explaining 'what is the reason.' Why does one who weeds or covers roots of כלאים get lashes? Because of maintaining, since רבי עקיבא says: even one who maintains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the ברייתא differently. The second half explains the first half instead of disagreeing with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed two תנאים who disagree. The גמרא says there is only one voice, רבי עקיבא's. The 'even one who maintains' line gives the reason for the lashes, so רבה's answer holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole teaching follows רבי עקיבא
It is giving the reason (the second part explains the first)
One who covers the roots with earth

steps.whatToRemember: רבה survives רב יוסף's challenge. Lashes for weeding כלאים are for maintaining (מקיים) the mixture, and the whole ברייתא is רבי עקיבא explaining his own reason.
steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, 'רבי עקיבא says: even one who maintains' is not a new opinion that disagrees with the first part. It is the reason for the first part.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Akiva,
and it is saying 'what is the reason':
phrases.notes: Read the last part as an explanation of the first part, not as an argument with it.

phrases.english: What is the reason that one who weeds and one who covers [roots] in כלאים
gets lashes? Because of maintaining,
for Rabbi Akiva says: even one who maintains [gets lashes].

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, וּמַאי טַעַם קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 13 and so keeps רבה's answer from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא as one author explaining his reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא has two opinions, and only רבי עקיבא holds מקיים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא is רבי עקיבא, and its last line gives the reason (מקיים) for the lashes in the first line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the 'מאי טעם קאמר' move. The גמרא can read a line that looks like a new opinion as the reason for the earlier line. Here that keeps רבה's view that weeding is חורש.

steps.title: What is רבי עקיבא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי עקיבא's rule that keeping כלאים growing earns lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said the whole ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who gives lashes even for keeping כלאים growing. Now it asks where in the תורה he learns this. This question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק plainly forbids sowing כלאים. Keeping them growing involves no new act of planting. So we need a source showing that keeping them is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (a request for a source or logic)
One who keeps or maintains something, here letting כלאים keep growing

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: He's asking for רבי עקיבא's source that even keeping כלאים growing is forbidden, like the end of the ברייתא in step 10 says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After making רבי עקיבא's view the basis of the whole ברייתא, the גמרא asks for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that keeping כלאים growing (קיום) is forbidden.

steps.title: The פסוק read as 'כלאים in your field, no'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word order of the פסוק that even keeping כלאים is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'Your field you shall not sow with כלאים.' From this I would only know that sowing is forbidden. Where do we learn that keeping them is also forbidden? The פסוק says: 'כלאים, your field, no.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא asks its own question, how we know keeping כלאים is forbidden, and answers by reading the words of the פסוק in a different grouping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading only forbids the act of sowing. The ברייתא joins the word כלאים to 'your field, no,' which yields 'your field shall not have כלאים.' That forbids having them there at all, even with no new action, and that is רבי עקיבא's source.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (from the plain words)
From where do we learn it?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns from the פסוק 'כלאים שדך לא' that just keeping כלאים in your field is forbidden. That is why even one who weeds or covers roots gets lashes.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Your field you shall not sow with mixed seeds,"
I have only one who sows;
from where do we learn one who maintains them?
The verse says: "Mixed seeds, your field, no."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, read as one phrase: 'your field shall not have כלאים.' That covers just having them there, not only planting them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'כלאים שדך לא' read together forbid having כלאים in one's field, which includes keeping them alive.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: watering a thirsty field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which permits watering a field that needs irrigation on חול המועד and in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: one may water a field that needs irrigation on חול המועד and in שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about כלאים is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the משנה's ruling to set up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that watering a field may count as a form of farm work, either sowing or plowing. Yet the משנה allows it both on חול המועד and in שביעית. Placing these two side by side prepares the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A thirsty field that needs artificial watering
The seventh year, when farm work is forbidden

phrases.english: We learned: One may water a field that needs irrigation
on the Festival and in the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: 'מועד' here means חול המועד, the in-between days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כלאים side topic and returns to the משנה as the base for a new challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may water a field that needs irrigation on חול המועד and in שביעית.

steps.title: How can watering be allowed in שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: On חול המועד the ban is only about effort, so the רבנן could allow it to prevent a loss. But in שביעית watering counts as sowing or plowing, and both are forbidden then.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for חול המועד: the problem there is only the effort, and where there is a loss the רבנן allowed it. But in שביעית, whether watering counts as sowing or as plowing, are sowing and plowing allowed in שביעית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It accepts the חול המועד part, but asks how the משנה can allow watering in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד the rule against work is a lighter ban about effort, so the רבנן could relax it to prevent a loss. In שביעית, both earlier views treat watering as real farm work: one calls it sowing and the other calls it plowing. Either way it is a forbidden act in שביעית, so how could the משנה permit it?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that (grants one part before challenging another)
Is it permitted? (a challenge meaning: surely not)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the חול המועד part at all. Its whole problem is only with שביעית.

phrases.english: Granted, the Festival:
it is because of exertion,
and where there is a loss, the Rabbis permitted it.
But the Sabbatical Year:
both according to the one who said it is because of sowing
and according to the one who said it is because of plowing,
phrases.notes: These are the two earlier views: רב יוסף said watering counts as sowing, and רבה said it counts as plowing.

phrases.english: are sowing and plowing permitted in the Sabbatical Year?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in step 17 to raise a challenge about שביעית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to water a thirsty field in שביעית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under both views watering is a real farm act (sowing or plowing), and those are forbidden in שביעית. Unlike חול המועד, it cannot be explained as a mere effort ban that the רבנן relaxed to prevent a loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of what exactly is forbidden in שביעית today, and how the משנה's permission can fit.

steps.title: אביי: The משנה Is Talking About שביעית Today, Following רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question: the משנה is speaking about שביעית in our time, and it follows the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The משנה is talking about שביעית in the present time, and it follows the opinion of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 18 about how watering could be allowed in שביעית. He says the משנה is only talking about שביעית nowadays, and it follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that working the land in שביעית is a Torah prohibition. אביי says that today, according to רבי, שביעית is only a rabbinic law. A rabbinic law leaves room for the רבנן to be lenient when a big loss is at stake.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh (שמיטה) year in our time, after the Temple period
A law made by the Sages, not directly from the Torah

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is talking about the Sabbatical Year in the present time,
and it follows the opinion of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁבִיעִית בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, וְרַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18 by narrowing the משנה to שביעית nowadays.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a time when the prohibition is only rabbinic, following a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Watering in שביעית is like sowing or plowing and is forbidden by the Torah, so the משנה could not allow it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals with שביעית today, which according to רבי is only דרבנן, so the Sages allowed watering to prevent a loss.

steps.title: רבי's Source: Release of Land Is Tied to Release of Debts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי reads the פסוק as linking the release of land to the release of money, which leads to the idea that שביעית today is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, the פסוק "And this is the manner of the release: release" speaks of two releases, the release of land and the release of money. When you release land, you release money. When you do not release land, you do not release money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי's view comes from. רבי says the פסוק ties two kinds of release together: resting the land and canceling debts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word "שמוט" teaches two releases, and the פסוק makes them depend on each other. Each one applies by Torah law only when the other does. This supports אביי's claim that, according to רבי, the release of land today is not a Torah law but only a rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: Release of land: not working the fields in the seventh year
Release of money: canceling loans in the seventh year

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, the release of land and the release of debts go together. That is the basis for saying שביעית today is only דרבנן.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita, Rabbi says:
"And this is the manner of the release: release."
The verse speaks of two releases:
one is the release of land,
and the other is the release of money.
When you release land,
you release money,
and when you do not release land,
you do not release money.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: וְזֶה דְּבַר הַשְּׁמִטָּה שָׁמוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's claim that, according to רבי, שביעית today is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי holds שביעית today is not a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי reads דברים 15:2 as linking the release of land with the release of money

steps.title: רבא: Even the Rabbis Agree, Since the Torah Forbade Only Main Labors
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a different answer: the משנה can follow even the רבנן, because the Torah forbade only the main categories of work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. The Merciful One forbade only the main categories of work...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer to the question from Step 18. He does not need to limit the משנה to רבי's view. His sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disagree with רבי and hold that שביעית is a Torah law even today. רבא says that is not a problem, because the Torah's ban covers only the main categories of work (אבות). Watering is not one of those main categories, so the Torah does not forbid it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the case can fit even this view)
The Sages who disagree with רבי
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with רבי's ברייתא. He is giving a separate answer that works even according to the רבנן, who hold שביעית is a Torah law today.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis;
the Merciful One forbade only the primary categories of labor,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the קשיא of Step 18, one that does not need אביי's limit to רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the scope of the Torah prohibition: only the main categories of work (אבות) are forbidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the רבנן hold שביעית is a Torah law today, watering should be forbidden by the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to the רבנן, the Torah forbade only the main categories of work, so watering can be allowed. The explanation continues past this point.
